cells.tense: Present — the pen is in your hand and you haven't rushed it.
cells.verb: holding what you already know until it's ready to be said
cells.place: in the spot where you decide which way to go
cells.ask: Let one decision you've been holding privately become something other people can stand on — say the 'this, not that' out loud and keep it standing. What comes back is a room where things make sense because you're in it.
cells.core:
You're deciding right now, and you're not rushing it. The direction is already clear inside you — you can feel which way it goes — and you're letting it sit a beat longer on purpose, not from doubt. When you do say it, it will come out whole. That pause is choosing; it just hasn't spoken yet.

There's a next step this is free to take, if you want it. The clarity you hold alone can become the thing others arrange themselves around. Let one decision you've been holding privately become something other people can stand on — say the 'this, not that' out loud and keep it standing. What comes back is a room where things make sense because you're in it.
cells.sheetLine: You know which way, and you're letting it ripen before you say it.

cells.tense: Future — bracing for a certainty that isn't coming.
cells.verb: holding the decision shut past the moment it was ready
cells.place: in the spot where you decide which way to go
cells.ask: Pick the direction you've been weighing and keep walking it through the days it feels wrong — let staying on it, not being sure of it, be the strength. What comes back is a knowing that proves itself by holding, and an easiness with the parts you can't see yet.
cells.core:
You're waiting to be sure before you move, and sure keeps not arriving. Somewhere ahead is a version where the choice is obvious and risk-free, and you're holding everything closed until you reach it — weighing again, checking again, keeping both doors open so long that neither one is a door anymore. The holding was meant to end in a yes. It's become the whole posture.

The way through isn't more weighing. Pick the direction you've been weighing and keep walking it through the days it feels wrong — let staying on it, not being sure of it, be the strength. What comes back is a knowing that proves itself by holding, and an easiness with the parts you can't see yet.
cells.sheetLine: You keep the decision closed waiting for a certainty that won't come.

cells.tense: Past — still choosing from a door that's already behind you.
cells.verb: skipping the inner pause and letting the old answer choose
cells.place: in the spot where you decide which way to go
cells.ask: Take one thing that already happened and stay with it until it's finished in you — picture how it actually went, all the way to the end, until you can feel what you'd want next. What comes back is a sense of direction that lands on its own, and comfort with what you don't know yet.
cells.core:
You're not stopping to check before you turn. The direction is getting set by whatever was decided before — the last time it went a certain way — and the inner moment where you'd weigh it fresh isn't happening. It doesn't feel like choosing; it feels like being carried. The knowing is still in you. It just isn't being consulted.

Pushing harder on the choice won't open it. Take one thing that already happened and stay with it until it's finished in you — picture how it actually went, all the way to the end, until you can feel what you'd want next. What comes back is a sense of direction that lands on its own, and comfort with what you don't know yet.
cells.sheetLine: You've stopped weighing; the old outcome is picking the direction.

cells.tense: Disowned present — the direction is set and you're calling it open.
cells.verb: already knowing which way, and presenting it as undecided
cells.place: in the spot where you decide which way to go
cells.ask: Put the decision you're already carrying on the table with one person it affects, and let what they give back count. What comes back is a knowing that lands without needing to be argued for.
cells.core:
You've already chosen. You can feel it — the way one option gets a little more room every time it comes up, the way your plans quietly assume it — but what you tell people, and maybe yourself, is that you're still thinking it over. The thinking is done. You're steering by it. The only thing not happening is the saying-so, and the people around you are being steered without having been told.

The fix is smaller than it feels. Put the decision you're already carrying on the table with one person it affects, and let what they give back count. What comes back is a knowing that lands without needing to be argued for.
cells.sheetLine: You've already decided. You're still calling it thinking.
